title: Maximum Valid Split Positions I
summary: Given an integer array nums, you can remove at most one element.
statement: Given an integer array nums, you can remove at most one element. Define arr as the remaining elements in their original order. A split position i in arr is valid if 0 <= i < m-1 and the greatest common divisor of the first i+1 elements equals the greatest common divisor of the remaining elements. An array of length 1 has no valid split positions. The score is the count of valid split positions. Return the highest possible score for arr.
constraints: Remove zero or one element while preserving order.
A split is valid when the GCD of its nonempty prefix equals the GCD of its nonempty suffix.
Return the maximum number of valid split positions after the optional removal.
hints: For any fixed remaining array, prefix and suffix GCD arrays score every split in linear time.
Evaluate the original and each possible one-element removal.
Build both GCD scans and count equal adjacent-side values.
The outer enumeration covers every permitted result; the inner scan checks every legal split exactly.
editorial: The outer enumeration covers every permitted result; the inner scan checks every legal split exactly.

A one-element result has no split positions.
